title: The Payer's Retroactive Window and the Days Counted on an Insured Plan of Care Gap
content:
**Payer program note — Insured Plan of Care.** Only the days the payer's retroactive window still reaches are counted toward a retroactive request:

1. Where the payer program accepts retroactive requests and the gap reaches back further than its retroactive window from today, only the days from the first day the window reaches — today less the retroactive window days — through the end of the gap are counted.
2. Where the payer program accepts no retroactive request, or no appointment funded by the plan has been attended since the gap began, no day is counted.
3. Otherwise every day of the gap is counted.

Attendance is read from the Appointment Series history of appointments funded by the plan.

| Payer program | Retroactive window (calendar days) | Accepts retroactive requests |
|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Plan of Care | 0 | No |
| Commercial High-Deductible Plan of Care | 0 | No |
| Commercial POS Plan of Care | 14 | Yes |
| Commercial HMO Plan of Care | 0 | No |
| Medicare Part B Plan of Care | 0 | No |
| Medicare Advantage Plan of Care | 0 | No |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | 30 | Yes |

## Worked boundary (hypothetical Commercial POS plan, window 14, today 2026-05-24)

The first day the window reaches is 2026-05-10 (today less 14 days).

| Gap | Funded appointment attended since the gap began | Days counted |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-05-01 through today | Yes | 15 (2026-05-10 through 2026-05-24) |
| 2026-05-10 through today | Yes | 15 — the gap does not reach back further than the window |
| 2026-05-11 through today | Yes | 14 |
| 2026-05-11 through today | No | 0 |

On the Commercial PPO Plan of Care, with a window of 0, no day is counted whatever the gap.
